blocks.text: BASIC EVALUATION

• Syncope/presyncope: frequency, associated fall/ injury/incontinence
• Exertional angina or known coronary artery diseas
• Look for reversible cause like drugs ( Beta-blockers, Calcium Channel
Blockers or digoxin)
• Known hypothyroidism or kidney disease
..  Sleep aponea
• Patient with an implanted pacemaker or other device

HISTORY
EXAMINATION
TESTS TO BE DONE

• Hypotension (SBP <90 mmHg), impaired consciousness or ongoing chest
pain
• Recurrent or ongoing syncope/presyncope
• Associated headache with or without neurologic deﬁcit (suspect
intracranial event)
• Patient with a pre-existing device
• If ECG available, evidence of any of the following
- Complete heart block
- Sinus node disease with pauses >3 s long
- Bradycardia (HR < 50 bpm)

1. TREATMENT OF ASSOCIATED CONDITIONS
- Suspected drug (BB or CCB) overdose:

• Withhold the drug
- Hyperkalemia(serum K+>6meq/l orwith ECG chages of hyperkalemia)
1.  Stop exogenous potassium, K sparing diuretics, NSAID, RAAS inhibitors
2. 10 ml of 10% calcium gluconate over 10 mins
3. IV insulin with glucose
4. IV sodabicarb
5. Salbutamol inhalation/ loop diuretics/ potassium binders

blocks.text: INDICATIONS FOR PERMANENT PACING

1. Rule out associated conditions
Drug toxicity (BB, CCB, clonidine, Lithium)
Renal dysfunction, hyperkalemia
Sleep apnea
2. Transthoracic echocardiography

AV CONDUCTION DISEASE
• Complete heart block, advanced AV
block, or Mobitz Type II block
• Associated neuromuscular disease

blocks.text: ADDITIONAL TESTING

1. SND with intact AV conduction
- Atrial-based single or dual chamber pacing
- VVI pacing is reasonable if symptoms are
infrequent
2. AV Conduction disease
- VVI/Dual chamber pacing in patients with
LVEF >50%
- CRT/LBBA pacing system pacing in patients
with LVEF <40%
